scenarios.question: Where should an AI triage system assist clinicians, and where must people retain control?
claims: AI may prioritise routine referrals only when a clinician can override its recommendation.
Patients must be told when AI materially influences the priority of their referral.
An independent subgroup performance audit must be completed before deployment.
Emergency referrals must never be downgraded solely on an AI recommendation.
scenarios.feedback: The nursing lead distinguished a usable override from a nominal one; the rural practitioner raised limited audit samples. Participants retained disagreement about the audit threshold rather than treating disclosure as consent.

scenarios.title: Should universities replace essays in the age of AI?
scenarios.question: How should universities assess learning when students can use generative AI?
claims: Students may use generative AI in assessed coursework if its role is disclosed.
Every degree must include an assessment where students explain their own reasoning orally.
AI-detector scores alone must never establish academic misconduct.
All take-home essays should be replaced with supervised examinations.
scenarios.feedback: The disability adviser identified accessibility limits to a universal oral requirement. The humanities lecturer explained what would be lost by replacing all essays. The panel increasingly opposed the blanket replacement while preserving disagreement about oral assessment.

Replacing every essay removes valuable research and revision skills.

scenarios.title: Protect the coastline—or help communities move?
scenarios.question: How should a coastal town balance flood protection, voluntary relocation and fairness?
claims: Residents in repeatedly flooded homes should be offered voluntary relocation grants.
Publicly funded coastal defences should be prioritised using property values alone.
Any relocation programme must include support for renters as well as owners.
New housing should be prohibited in the highest-risk flood zone.
scenarios.feedback: The tenant organiser exposed the gap between property compensation and displacement costs. Participants rejected property value as the sole criterion more strongly, but housing-supply concerns sustained disagreement about a building prohibition.

people.opening: Relocation can break relationships built over decades. A nominal choice is not voluntary when services are withdrawn first. Property values alone privilege wealthy places and miss community losses. Renters also lose homes, social networks and access to services. A blanket prohibition may worsen shortages where few alternative sites exist.
